interactions.label: Which feature most reliably distinguishes a laceration from an incised wound on

params.question: Which feature most reliably distinguishes a laceration from an incised wound on the scalp?

answers.text: Lacerations bleed more profusely than incised wounds

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both lacerations and incised wounds on the scalp can bleed profusely due to the rich scalp vasculature. Bleeding volume alone does not distinguish the two.

answers.text: Presence of tissue bridges across the wound depth

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Tissue bridges — intact strands of connective tissue, nerves, or vessels spanning the wound — form because blunt force tears tissue unevenly. A sharp weapon cuts cleanly through all layers, leaving no bridges.
Clean, straight margins are characteristic of incised wounds (sharp force). Lacerations have irregular, torn margins due to blunt force disruption.

answers.text: Incised wounds are always deeper than lacerations

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Depth depends on the force applied and weapon characteristics, not on the wound type alone. Both can be superficial or deep.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: tissue bridges form when blunt force tears tissue unevenly, leaving intact strands across the wound. Sharp weapons cut cleanly through all layers.
Tissue bridges are the single most reliable feature to distinguish a laceration (blunt force) from an incised wound (sharp force) — a key forensic distinction.

interactions.label: A penetrating wound to the neck causes rapid death. Which of the following is a

params.question: A penetrating wound to the neck causes rapid death. Which of the following is a recognised mechanism of death in such injuries?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Fat embolism is classically associated with long bone fractures (femur, tibia), not cervical vertebral injuries. The neck's lethal mechanisms are vascular, airway, and neurological.

answers.text: Airway obstruction from blood or tissue oedema compressing the trachea

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Neck injuries can obstruct the airway directly (tracheal damage) or indirectly (haematoma compressing the trachea or larynx), making this one of the three major mechanisms of death alongside exsanguination and neurological disruption.
Oesophageal perforation in the neck can cause mediastinitis, but tension pneumoperitoneum (air in the peritoneal cavity) is not a recognised mechanism of death from neck wounds.
Myoglobin-induced renal failure occurs in crush syndrome from prolonged compression of large muscle masses, not from neck injuries.

overallFeedback.feedback: Neck injuries kill through three mechanisms: massive haemorrhage from great vessel injury, airway obstruction from tracheal damage or compressive haematoma, and neurological disruption from spinal cord injury.
The three mechanisms of death in neck injuries are: exsanguination (carotid/jugular injury), airway obstruction (tracheal compression or haematoma), and neurological disruption (spinal cord injury).

interactions.label: In a pedestrian struck by a car, a transverse fracture of the tibia is found 45

params.question: In a pedestrian struck by a car, a transverse fracture of the tibia is found 45 cm from the sole of the foot. What is the primary forensic significance of this measurement?

answers.text: It estimates the speed of the vehicle at the time of impact

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Vehicle speed is estimated from the severity and pattern of overall injuries, not from the height of a single fracture. The fracture height corresponds to bumper position.

answers.text: It indicates the bumper height, helping identify the type of vehicle involved

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The bumper fracture height measured from the sole corresponds to the vehicle's bumper height. This helps identify whether the vehicle was a sedan, SUV, or truck — crucial for accident reconstruction and vehicle identification in hit-and-run cases.

answers.text: It determines whether the victim was walking or running at impact

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The victim's gait does not significantly alter the height of the bumper fracture, which is determined by the fixed bumper-to-ground clearance of the vehicle.

answers.text: It confirms the injury was caused by a vehicle rather than a fall

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While bumper fractures are characteristic of vehicular impact, the forensic value of measuring the exact height is vehicle identification (bumper height varies by vehicle type), not merely confirming vehicular cause.

overallFeedback.feedback: The bumper fracture is a transverse tibial/fibular fracture at the bumper's contact height. Measuring this distance from the sole helps identify the vehicle type — critical in accident reconstruction and hit-and-run cases.
The bumper fracture height from the sole matches the vehicle's bumper height — a key measurement for identifying the offending vehicle in hit-and-run investigations.

interactions.label: In crush syndrome, the life-threatening metabolic complications — hyperkalaemia

params.question: In crush syndrome, the life-threatening metabolic complications — hyperkalaemia and acute renal failure — develop primarily after the compression is released and the victim is rescued.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Although muscle destruction occurs during compression, the systemic crisis happens after release: myoglobin and potassium from destroyed muscle flood into the circulation, causing potentially fatal hyperkalaemia and acute renal failure.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. During compression, ischaemic muscle damage accumulates locally. Upon release, the products of rhabdomyolysis — potassium, myoglobin, and phosphate — flood the systemic circulation, causing hyperkalaemia (cardiac arrest risk) and myoglobinuric acute renal failure.

interactions.label: A man is struck on the left temporal region. Autopsy reveals a left temporal epi

params.question: A man is struck on the left temporal region. Autopsy reveals a left temporal epidural haematoma and a right frontal lobe contusion. The right frontal contusion is best classified as:

answers.text: A coup injury caused by direct force transmission through the skull

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Coup injuries occur at the site of impact. The right frontal lobe is contralateral to the left temporal impact — this is not a coup injury.

answers.text: A contre-coup injury caused by brain displacement opposite to the impact site

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. When the left temporal region is struck, the brain shifts rightward due to inertia and impacts the right side of the anterior cranial fossa, producing a contre-coup contusion on the right frontal lobe.

answers.text: A diffuse axonal injury from rotational acceleration of the brain

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Diffuse axonal injury involves widespread white-matter shearing, not a focal contusion. This localised right frontal contusion is a classic contre-coup pattern.

answers.text: A secondary ischaemic injury from raised intracranial pressure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Secondary ischaemic injury from raised ICP produces diffuse damage, not a focal contusion. A well-defined contusion contralateral to the impact site is the hallmark of contre-coup injury.

overallFeedback.feedback: Contre-coup contusions occur opposite to the impact site — the brain's inertia causes it to strike the inner skull on the far side. This pattern helps the forensic physician reconstruct the direction of the blow.
The combination of coup fracture and EDH at the impact site with a contre-coup contusion on the opposite side is a classic forensic finding that confirms the direction of force application.
